9	/-!
10	# β1 — Pic⁰ commutes with the base-field colimit `K_s = colim k''` (DAT-G0 probe)
11	
12	**Deliverable of the DAT-G0 β1 feasibility probe** (mini-spec `informal/spec-datg0.md`
13	§4.3, landing note I-0259).  β1 is the SOLE avatar-less brick gating the DAT-G0 route:
14	*does the degree-zero Picard functor `pic0` commute with the filtered colimit
15	`K_s = colim_{k''} k''` of the base field (`k''` ranging over finite separable
16	subextensions of `K_s/k'`)?*  This file states β1 precisely against the landed
17	`pic0Subgroup`/`pic0TypeFunctor` API, records the **verdict**, and lands the load-bearing
18	**reduction** to a single pinned residual.
19	
20	## Verdict: **YES — provable-in-tree (L), route-pinned; NOT obstructed, NOT the fallback**
21	
22	The hard search DOWNGRADES β1 from "XL, no landed avatar" to "L, reduction fully landed,
23	one analytic residual", because the base-field-change functoriality of `pic0` is **already
24	a landed NATURAL ISOMORPHISM**:
25	
26	* `pic0Theta` / `pic0ThetaType` (`Picard/Pic0ThetaAssembly.lean`):
27	  `pic0Functor (C_L) ≅ (Over.map σ).op ⋙ pic0Functor C`, for an **arbitrary** field
28	  extension `k → L` (`σ = Spec.map (algebraMap k L)`), with **no** finiteness / separability
29	  / Galois content.  I.e. the Pic⁰ functor over the base-changed field `L` is the FIXED
30	  challenge-base functor `pic0Functor C` precomposed with the pushforward `(Over.map σ).op`.
31	
32	This collapses β1 onto the **single fixed functor** `pic0TypeFunctor C` over the challenge
33	base `k`.  After rebasing every stage by `pic0Theta`, the varying-field colimit
34	`colim_{k''} pic0(C_{k''})(T''_{k''}) → pic0(C_{K_s})(T''_{K_s})` becomes an internal
35	statement in the single category `Over (Spec (.of k))`:
36	
37	> **β1 (fixed-base form, the honest content):** the fixed functor `pic0TypeFunctor C`
38	> sends the cofiltered limit of test schemes `S_{K_s} = lim_{k''} S_{k''}`
39	> (`S_{k''} := (Over.map σ_{k''}).obj T''_{k''}`, all `k`-schemes, affine transition maps
40	> since `Spec k''' → Spec k''` is affine, qcqs) to the filtered colimit of its values.
41	
42	The reduction *(raw base-field colimit)  ⟸  (fixed-base cofiltered-limit preservation)*
43	is **fully mechanical from landed + mathlib machinery**:
44	`pic0ThetaType` (the componentwise natural iso) + mathlib's colimit transport across a
45	natural iso (`CategoryTheory.Limits.preservesColimit_of_natIso`,
46	`IsColimit.equivOfNatIsoOfIso`).  See `pic0TypeFunctor_baseChange_iso` and
47	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit` below.
48	
49	### The sole pinned residual (the analytic heart, avatar in hand)
50	
51	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C` — that `pic0TypeFunctor C` (FIXED base `k`) is
52	locally of finite presentation *as a functor*.  On **affine** tests `overSpec k A` this is
53	exactly:
54	
55	> the affine relative-Picard plus construction `PicEtAff C A` (hence its degree-zero
56	> subgroup `pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)`) **commutes with filtered colimits of the test
57	> algebra `A`**,
58	
59	which rides **finite presentation of the proper smooth curve `C/k`**.  Named avatars
60	(mathlib, `.lake-packages/mathlib` v4.31.0, verified this pass):
61	
62	* `CommRingCat.preservesColimit_coyoneda_of_finitePresentation`
63	  (`Algebra/Category/Ring/FinitePresentation.lean:144`) — `Hom_R(S,−)` preserves filtered
64	  colimits for finitely-presented `S`;
65	* `RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_eq_comp_ι_app_of_isColimit` (`:81`, existence /
66	  surjectivity) + `RingHom.EssFiniteType.exists_comp_map_eq_of_isColimit` (`:45`,
67	  uniqueness / injectivity);
68	* scheme level: `Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`
69	  (`AlgebraicGeometry/AffineTransitionLimit.lean:1177`, EXISTENCE) +
70	  `Scheme.exists_hom_hom_comp_eq_comp_of_locallyOfFiniteType` (`:686`, UNIQUENESS) +
71	  `Scheme.exists_isAffineOpen_preimage_eq` (`:1058`) / `exists_isOpenCover_and_isAffine`
72	  (`:1078`) for spreading the affine opens & sections of `S_{K_s} = lim S_{k''}` back to a
73	  finite stage.
74	
75	This residual is **`divRep`-free** (it is intrinsic to `C/k`, needing neither the Jacobian
76	nor `rep_{K_s}`), sized M–L; it is NOT a one-probe proof, hence the probe verdict is
77	**YES-PINNED** rather than **YES-LANDED**.  What DAT-G0's β brick now consumes:
78	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C` (this file) ⟹ β1 ⟹ (with α + the LANDED
79	`AffineTransitionLimit`/`Ring.FinitePresentation` spreading) β2's descent of `rep_{K_s}` to
80	a finite stage `k'`.
81	
82	## Main declarations
83	
84	* `pic0TypeFunctor_baseChange_iso` — the landed rebasing: `pic0TypeFunctor (C_L)` is the
85	  fixed-base functor precomposed with the pushforward (a repackaging of `pic0ThetaType`,
86	  machine-checked here in the exact form the colimit argument consumes).
87	* `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit` — the β1 residual, as a named `Prop` over the FIXED
88	  base: `pic0TypeFunctor C` preserves the colimit (in `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ`) of every
89	  cofiltered limit of qcqs test schemes with affine transition maps.  The pinned target of
90	  the DAT-G0 implementation lane.
91	* `pic0_baseField_preserves_of_fixedBase` — the reduction: the residual for the fixed base
92	  `C` transports along `pic0ThetaType` to base-field-colimit preservation for `C_L`,
93	  i.e. β1 for the base-changed curve follows from the fixed-base residual.
94	-/

112	functor over the base-changed field `L` is the FIXED challenge-base functor
113	`pic0TypeFunctor C` precomposed with the pushforward `(Over.map σ).op`
114	(`σ = Spec.map (algebraMap k L)`) — verbatim the landed natural isomorphism
115	`pic0ThetaType`.  This is the identity that collapses the β1 base-field colimit onto the
116	single fixed functor `pic0TypeFunctor C`: every stage `pic0(C_{k''})` is `pic0 C` read on
117	the pushed-forward test, so the varying-field colimit is a cofiltered *limit of test
118	schemes* over the fixed base `k`. -/
119	noncomputable def pic0TypeFunctor_baseChange_iso :
120	    pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)
121	      ≅ (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).op
122	          ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C :=
123	  pic0ThetaType k L C
124	
125	/-! ## The β1 residual (pinned) and the reduction to the fixed base -/
126	
127	/-- **The β1 residual** — the sole avatar-less analytic heart this probe pins.  The FIXED
128	challenge-base functor `pic0TypeFunctor C` is *locally of finite presentation as a functor*:
129	it sends the colimit (in `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ`) of every cofiltered limit of qcqs test
130	schemes with affine transition maps to the filtered colimit of its values.  Equivalently,
131	on affine tests, `PicEtAff C A` commutes with filtered colimits of the test algebra `A`
132	(finite presentation of `C/k`).  Named avatars: see the module docstring
133	(`preservesColimit_coyoneda_of_finitePresentation`,
134	`exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`).  Pinned target of the DAT-G0
135	implementation lane; `divRep`-free, intrinsic to `C/k`. -/
136	def Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit : Prop :=
137	  ∀ ⦃J : Type u⦄ [SmallCategory J] [IsCofiltered J] (S : J ⥤ Over (Spec (.of k))),
138	    (∀ ⦃i j : J⦄ (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (S.map f).left) →
139	    (∀ i, CompactSpace (S.obj i).left) →
140	    (∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (S.obj i).left) →
141	    ∀ [HasLimit S], PreservesColimit S.op (pic0TypeFunctor C)
142	
143	/-- **The β1 reduction (load-bearing core, LANDED).**  The base-field-colimit
144	compatibility of `pic0` at `L` follows, for *any* diagram `K` of `L`-tests, from the SAME
145	compatibility of the FIXED challenge-base functor read on the pushed-forward tests — because
146	`pic0TypeFunctor (C_L)` is `(Over.map σ).op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C` up to the landed natural
147	iso `pic0ThetaType`, and colimit preservation transports along a natural iso
148	(`preservesColimit_of_natIso`).  This is the step that carries the fixed-base residual
149	`Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit` to β1 for the base-changed curve `C_{K_s}`. -/
150	theorem preservesColimit_pic0TypeFunctor_baseChange {J : Type u} [Category.{u} J]
151	    (K : J ⥤ (Over (Spec (.of L)))ᵒᵖ)
152	    [PreservesColimit K ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).op
153	        ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C)] :
154	    PreservesColimit K (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
155	  preservesColimit_of_natIso K (pic0TypeFunctor_baseChange_iso C L).symm
156	
157	end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity

/-!
# DAT-B B-5: from pointwise coverage to the sieve condition

`Picard/Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity.lean` reduced B-6 to `ChartsCoverLocally`, whose statement
is *sieve-theoretic*: for every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the supremum
of the per-chart image sieves is a Zariski covering sieve.  The dat-b row calls that "B-5
verbatim" and says a producer discharges it "by exhibiting one open neighbourhood and one
index per point of `T`".

**That last sentence was a claim about a bridge nobody had written.**  What B-5's geometry
produces is pointwise: for each point `t` of the test, an open `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and a
chart point over `W` whose class restricts to `s`.  What `ChartsCoverLocally` asks for is
membership of a Grothendieck topology.  The two are connected by a *cover construction* —
`Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers` at the family `{W t}` indexed by the points of `T` — and the
connection is what this file supplies.

## Why the bridge is not bookkeeping the producer can inline

Three things have to line up, and each is a place a lane would stall:

* the cover must be indexed by a type in the right universe.  Indexing by the points of `T`
  works (`↥T : Type u` for `T : Scheme.{u}`) and is the *only* index available before any
  geometry is known — a producer that tries to index by a chosen finite subcover needs
  quasi-compactness, which no row assumes;
* `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` asks for `Presieve.ofArrows 𝒰.X 𝒰.f ≤ S.arrows`, i.e. a
  statement about the *presieve generated by the cover maps*, so the per-point witness has to
  be produced after destructing `ofArrows` — which binds the point, not an arbitrary map into
  `T`.  This is where the pointwise data is consumed;
* the per-point index makes the target sieve a *supremum*, and `le_iSup` is what turns "some
  chart works at `t`" into "the supremum contains `W t`".  Nothing forces one index to work
  at every point, which is the chart-parameter heterogeneity the dat-b row records — here it
  costs literally nothing, because `iSup` is what the statement already had.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise` — **the bridge**, stated for an
  arbitrary family of sieves: pointwise opens with a per-point index give the supremum sieve
  covering status.  No presheaf, no chart, no `pic⁰`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` — `ChartsCoverLocally` from exactly the
  data B-5 produces: per test point, an open neighbourhood, an index, and a chart point over
  that open with the right class.  **This is what a coverage lane owes, and nothing more.**

the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf

/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**

If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
Zariski covering sieve of `T`.

The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.

Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)

/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.

field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
it, and every point `t` of `T`:

  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is

* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the

* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.

Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.

and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.

written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/

    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
  intro T s
  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩

remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`

    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),

/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening

A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/

variable (C) in
/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**

The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.

**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩

end

18	
19	For a **separable algebraic** extension `K/k` (the case `K = K_s` a separable closure is the
20	DAT-G0 target), the finite subextensions form a **directed system** whose supremum is all of
21	`K`.  Concretely:
22	
23	* `FinSubext k K` — the index: finite(-dimensional) `k`-subextensions `k''` of `K`, ordered by
24	  inclusion.  It is **nonempty** and **directed** (`instNonemptyFinSubext`,
25	  `directed_finSubext`), so `(FinSubext k K)ᵒᵖ` is `IsCofiltered` — the shape the residual's
26	  `[IsCofiltered J]` binder consumes.
27	* `iSup_finSubext_eq_top` — `⨆ k'', k'' = ⊤`, i.e. **`K = colim k''`** at the lattice level.
28	* `coe_iSup_finSubext` — the colimit-is-**union** identity `↑(⨆ k'', k'') = ⋃ k'', ↑k''`
29	  (`IntermediateField.coe_iSup_of_directed`): every element of `K` already lives at a finite
30	  stage.  This is the honest content of "`K_s = colim k''`": the test-scheme limit
31	  `S_{K_s} = lim S_{k''}` is `Spec` of this filtered colimit of fields.
32	* `isSeparable_finSubext` — every stage `k''/k` is **separable** (`Algebra.IsSeparable`,
33	  inherited from `K/k` by `Algebra.isSeparable_tower_bot_of_isSeparable`); with
34	  `IntermediateField.isSeparable_iSup` the colimit is separable, so this is genuinely the
35	  system of *finite separable* subextensions of `K_s/k`.
36	
37	All native `k`-algebra / scalar-tower instances come from the `IntermediateField` API
38	(`Algebra k k''`, `IsScalarTower k k'' K`), per the I-0255 tower-diamond wall — no composite

41	## The β1 residual (pinned — `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`, in `PicRepColimitCompat`)

noncomputable def relThetaResSide :

      (relThetaSections C R π a →ₗ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, W))

  | true, _, hW => relThetaResSnd a (le_inf le_top hW)

lemma relThetaResSide_true {W : (relCurve C R).Opens}

    relThetaResSide a true hW x = (relCurve C R).resHom (le_inf le_top hW) x.val.2 := rfl

lemma resHom_relThetaResSide (b : Bool) {W W' : (relCurve C R).Opens}
    (hW : W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π b) (h' : W' ≤ W) (x : relThetaSections C R π a) :
    (relCurve C R).resHom h' (relThetaResSide a b hW x)
      = relThetaResSide a b (h'.trans hW) x := by
  cases b <;> exact Scheme.resHom_resHom _ _ _

/-- **The matching unit of an ordered pair of sides** on an open below both pinned
charts: `1` on equal sides, the theta cocycle (resp. its inverse) across the charts. -/
noncomputable def relThetaSideUnit :
    ∀ (b b' : Bool) {W : (relCurve C R).Opens},
      W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π b ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b' → Γ(relCurve C R, W)ˣ
  | false, false, _, _ => 1
  | false, true, _, hW => (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hW (relThetaCocycle C R π a)
  | true, false, _, hW =>

        (le_inf (hW.trans inf_le_right) (hW.trans inf_le_left))
        (relThetaCocycle C R π a))⁻¹
  | true, true, _, _ => 1

components of a global theta section differ by the side matching unit
(`relThetaSections_matching` in side-uniform form). -/
lemma relThetaResSide_matching (b b' : Bool) {W : (relCurve C R).Opens}
    (hW : W ≤ relPinnedChart C R π b ⊓ relPinnedChart C R π b')

        * relThetaResSide a b' (hW.trans inf_le_right) x := by
  cases b <;> cases b'
  · rw [show relThetaSideUnit a false false hW = 1 from rfl, Units.val_one, one_mul]
  · exact relThetaSections_matching a x hW
  · have key := relThetaSections_matching a x
      (le_inf (hW.trans inf_le_right) (hW.trans inf_le_left))
    change relThetaResSide a true (hW.trans inf_le_left) x

            (relThetaCocycle C R π a))⁻¹
          * relThetaResSide a false (hW.trans inf_le_right) x
    rw [Units.eq_inv_mul_iff_mul_eq]
    exact key.symm
  · rw [show relThetaSideUnit a true true hW = 1 from rfl, Units.val_one, one_mul]

/-- **The (C2) effectivity theorem** (recon §0.3; Kleiman `th:cmp` Part 2, the descent
of the rigidified pair): for a module-finite faithfully flat cover `A → B` of the test
algebra of a curve point `σ`, every Čech Picard class on the cover curve `X_B` that is
rigidified along the base-changed section (`hrig`) and has equal coprojection pullbacks
on the curve over `B ⊗[A] B` (`hdesc`) descends along the cover inclusion:
`∃ M, cg^* M = L`. -/
theorem exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq [Module.Finite A B]
    (L : (XB).CechPic)
    (hrig : Over.IsRigidified
      (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId A B).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ) L)
    (hdesc : Scheme.CechPic.map (u₁) L = Scheme.CechPic.map (u₂) L) :
    ∃ M : (XA).CechPic, Scheme.CechPic.map (cg) M = L := by

  rw [show (Quot.mk _ γ : (XB).unitsH1 𝒩)
    = CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.class γ from rfl] at hrig hdesc ⊢

variable (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- **Surjectivity of the unit of the étale plus construction over a section-admitting
field test** (Kleiman 2.5(2), axiom (C2) — the campaign headline): if the curve admits
a `K`-point `σ`, every class of `PicEtAff C K` comes from a relative Picard class.

A representative on an étale cover of `Spec K` is refined to a finite separable field
extension (field cofinality); the rigidification layer produces a rigidified Čech
representative whose descent equation holds on the nose; the (C2) effectivity theorem
descends it along the cover inclusion; and the `relPicMk`/`mk`-calculus identifies the
descended class's unit with the original plus class. -/
theorem PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    Function.Surjective (PicEtAff.unit C K) := by
  intro q
  induction q using PicEtAff.ind with | _ E x
  classical
  -- ### refine the representing cover to a finite separable field extension
  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hLalg, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨f⟩⟩ :=
    E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
  set F : Algebra.EtaleCover K := Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField (K := K) L with hF
  set g : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] F.Carrier :=
    ((Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toAlgHom).comp f with hg
  set y : descentClasses C F := descentMap C g x with hy
  have hq : PicEtAff.mk C E x = PicEtAff.mk C F y :=
    (PicEtAff.mk_descentMap C g x).symm
  haveI : Module.Finite K F.Carrier :=
    Module.Finite.equiv (R := K) (M := L)
      (Algebra.EtaleCover.ofFieldEquiv (K := K) L).symm.toLinearEquiv
  -- ### a rigidified representative of the descent class (G1)
  obtain ⟨Lc, hrig, hLcrep⟩ := relPic.exists_isRigidified_rep
    (Over.overSpecMap ((Algebra.ofId K F.Carrier).restrictScalars k) ≫ σ)
    (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
  have hmem : relPicMk C (overSpec k F.Carrier) Lc ∈ descentClasses C F := by
    rw [hLcrep]
    exact y.2
  -- ### the on-the-nose descent equation (the rigidified transport keystone)
  have hdesc0 := Over.IsRigidified.cechPicMap_doubleInl_eq_doubleInr σ hmem hrig
  have hinl : doubleInl (k := k) F = tensorInl (k := k) (A := K) (B := F.Carrier) :=
    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
  have hinr : doubleInr (k := k) F = tensorInr (k := k) (A := K) (B := F.Carrier) :=
    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
  rw [hinl, hinr] at hdesc0
  -- ### the effectivity theorem
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := Over.exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq C σ Lc hrig hdesc0
  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M, ?_⟩
  -- ### the `mk`-calculus close
  rw [PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C F (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M)]
  rw [hq]
  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C F) (Subtype.ext ?_)
  change relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId K F.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
      (relPicMk C (overSpec k K) M) = (y : relPic C (overSpec k F.Carrier))
  rw [relPicAlgMap, relPicMap_mk, hM, hLcrep]

/-- **The unit of the étale plus construction is an isomorphism over a
section-admitting field test** — étale separatedness (C1) plus effectivity (C2):
`relPic C (Spec K) ≃* PicEtAff C K`. -/
noncomputable def PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (σ : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    relPic C (overSpec k K) ≃* PicEtAff C K :=
  MulEquiv.ofBijective (PicEtAff.unit C K)
    ⟨PicEtAff.unit_injective C K, PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section C K σ⟩
